title: Read a Result
summary: No Model to build this time — just the Results and Checks panels, and what each row means once you have solved something.

steps.title: Solve produces a Result
steps.explain: Pressing Solve runs the current Step and attaches a Result to the Model. Nothing else in FEM Lab produces one — not opening an example, not editing the Journal.

steps.title: The Results tab
steps.explain: The Results tab's Extremes table lists every field's minimum and maximum, and where in the Model each occurs. Click a row's location to jump the viewer there.

steps.title: Reactions balance the applied load
steps.explain: Always check this first: the sum of the reactions at every constraint should equal the sum of the applied loads, to numerical precision. If it does not, something upstream is wrong — a load on the wrong Set, a constraint that is not doing what you think — and no stress number downstream is trustworthy until it does.

steps.title: The Checks tab
steps.explain: Checks groups four kinds of question: well-posedness (is there a body, a material, a constraint, a load?), mesh quality (element shape, aspect ratio), a cost estimate (DOF, memory, predicted time), and the assumption log — every default the solver used that you did not set explicitly.

steps.title: A Result goes stale
steps.explain: Editing the Model after a Result exists — a different mesh size, a moved load — dims the contours and marks the Result stale. The Journal keeps both the edit and the old Result side by side; Re-solve brings them back in sync. Nothing is silently out of date.
